counterfactual_missing_items: explicit statement that the initial shave biopsy was from the left lower eyelid lesion rather than the left cheek
explicit statement that the subsequent infiltrative biopsy was from the same lesion
explicit statement that the BCC is the cause of the cicatricial socket changes rather than a separate anophthalmic socket syndrome
decisive_items: nodular BCC of the left cheek
elevated, pearly lesion on the left lower eyelid
response.rationale: C1 uniquely integrates the histologic subtypes (nodular and infiltrative) with the left lower eyelid location, matching the pearly lesion and biopsy findings. R3 is correct but incomplete because it omits subtype and anatomic specificity. R1 and R2 describe secondary cicatricial/socket complications but do not account for the biopsied BCC.

rejected.why: Anophthalmic socket syndrome explains prosthesis extrusion and conjunctival shortening but does not account for the pearly lesion or nodular/infiltrative BCC on biopsy; it is a secondary complication.
Cicatricial ectropion explains eyelid skin contracture and scleral show but is a downstream effect and does not address the growing pearly lesion or BCC pathology.
